text.p: The following are top headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Alberta Tories reject health charter: Delegates to policy conference defeat proposal to guarantee timely access to certain medical treatments.
- Ontario to target student debt: Default rates 'unacceptably high.'
- Union, Chrysler in nasty dispute: Canadian Auto Workers union's real target is General Motors.
- World Cup of Hockey: Just a setback for Canada, or is an overhaul needed? Don't read too much into one game, Fleury says, but U.S. coach wonders if Canadian program needs to be revamped.
- Padania says arrivederci Roma: The birth of a mythical state, however symbolic, is bred of discontent.
- Newsprint prices plunge: 'Horrified' analysts say bigger production cuts needed to slow 'fastest, biggest' drop yet.
- Lehndorff Tandem Group postpones proxy war: Seeks rulings in MD Realty deal.
- Olivetti at the crossroads: The next few weeks are crucial for the Italian conglomerate as it fights to remain intact.

- Microsoft brings TV to Internet. Microsoft Corp has confirmed that it will use technology being unveiled today by Toronto-based Digital Renaissance Inc to broadcast original, interactive television programming over the Internet.
- Sound of bulls' hooves fading for pros: The bears continue to advance on the Canadian stock market.
- Markets roar ahead as inflation wanes: Stock markets set closing records and bonds surge as U.S. reports suggest little threat from inflation. In Canada, there may be room for a rate cut.

- Provincial trade pact starting to crumble. The British Columbia government is on the verge of repudiating Canada's three-month-old interprovincial trade agreement because of a dispute with New Brunswick.
